standard_prerequisites: Mitschi's theorem (Theorem Mi, printed (2.11)): the differential Galois group is topologically generated by the local differential Galois groups at the singular points.
Schlesinger's theorem (Theorem reg, printed (2.4)): at a regular singular point the monodromy group is Zariski dense in the local differential Galois group.
The NVE_1 system (fve) (printed (3.2)): the explicit four-dimensional first-order system along the particular solution.

Standard regular-singularity facts: a fundamental solution has the form P(t) t^A with P holomorphic and A constant, and the monodromy is e^{2 pi i A}; the formal monodromy around t = infinity is the inverse of the monodromy around t = 0.

Ramis's theorem (Theorem Ra, printed (2.10)) as the frame for the no-Stokes case: when no non-trivial Stokes phenomena are observed, the local Galois group is generated topologically by the formal monodromy and the exponential torus.
core_obligations: The connected component (G_1)^0 of the unit element of the differential Galois group G_1 of the (NVE)_1 is Abelian; explicitly (G_1)^0 is contained in the diagonal group { diag(mu^{-1}, mu^{-1}, mu, mu) : mu in C^* } - it coincides with the exponential torus T_infty when alpha in Q and is generated by the formal monodromy M-hat_infty and T_infty when alpha notin Q.
proof_roadmap: Display the explicit fundamental matrix solution Phi(t) of (fve) and identify the two singular points t = 0 (regular) and t = infinity (irregular); by Mitschi's theorem G_1 is topologically generated by the local groups G_0 and G_infinity.

Determine G_0: write Phi = P(t) t^A near the origin with explicit P(t) and A = diag(alpha-1, alpha-1, -alpha-1, -alpha-1); by Schlesinger's theorem G_0 is the closure of the group generated by M_0 = e^{2 pi i A}; run the three cases (alpha in Q \ Z: finite cyclic, (G_0)^0 trivial; alpha in Z: trivial; alpha notin Q: the full diagonal torus).

Determine G_infinity: factor Phi = H_1(t) t^{Lambda_1} exp(Q_1 t) with explicit H_1, Lambda_1, Q_1; since no non-trivial Stokes phenomena occur, G_infinity is generated topologically by the formal monodromy M-hat_infinity = M_0^{-1} and the explicit exponential torus T_infinity.
Conclude G_1 coincides with G_infinity and read off (G_1)^0 in both arithmetic cases; in either case it lies in the explicit diagonal group, which is Abelian.
